question.leadin: Democrat Pat Schroeder described this man's presidency as "Teflon-coated" because "nothing sticks to him."
question.text: Name this president who somehow survived scandals like the Iran-Contra Affair during his two terms in office in the 1980s.
question.clue: This man's press secretary James Brady was permanently disabled after being injured when John Hinckley Jr. tried to assassinate this man.

swap.leadin: Name these American generals from World War II.
swap.text: The U.S. Army's chief of staff during the war was this man, who served as Harry Truman's Secretary of State and earned a Nobel Peace Prize for his "European Recovery" plan to repair the war's damage.
swap.clue: One king with this name survived the Forty-Five Jacobite Rising, and was the final monarch of his country to lead troops in battle.

question.leadin: Give the following about containment, the official US policy for stopping the spread of communism.
question.text: This President, who served between Ford and Reagan, tried to shift from containment to a more pacifist foreign policy until the Soviets invaded Afghanistan in 1979. He won a Nobel Peace Prize in 2002, in part for his work with Habitat for Humanity.
question.clue: This President lost his reelection bid in a race that featured Independent candidate John B. Anderson.

swap.text: Clinton's victory in the 1992 election has been linked to this third-party candidate, whose campaign drew voters away from Bush. This billionaire owner of Electronic Data Systems died in 2019.
swap.answerHtml: Ross Perot (accept Henry Ross Perot; accept Henry Ray Perot)
swap.clue: This man promised there would be a "giant sucking sound" as jobs went to Mexico when speaking out against NAFTA.

question.leadin: This controversy centered around a violation of the three separate pieces of legislation aimed at preventing US involvement in Nicaragua.
question.text: Name this controversy that saw the US sell guns to a certain Middle Eastern country, and use the profits to fund a group of rebels fighting the Nicaraguan Sandinistas.
question.clue: The plan, in violation of the Boland Amendment, was conceived by Robert McFarlane.

swap.leadin: He was readmitted to the Massachusetts bar after serving three and a half years in prison.
swap.text: Identify this man accused by Whittaker Chambers of being a Soviet spy within the State Department. Character witnesses during his trial included two Supreme Court justices among numerous other dignitaries.
swap.clue: Along with Harry Dexter White, he was implicated by the Moynihan commission using information from the Venona project.

question.text: Some have argued that Reagan should not be inducted because he surrendered names of union members to this anti-communist organization during the Second Red Scare. The Hollywood Ten testified before this organization.
question.clue: The "Hollywood Ten" were blacklisted for refusing to testify in front of this group, whose members included Jerry Voorhis and Richard Nixon.

swap.leadin: Name the following related to the Second Red Scare.
swap.text: This man who served as head counsel of the Army during the Army-McCarthy hearings is well-known for defending Fred Fisher while attacking McCarthy with the phrase "Have you no sense of decency?"

question.leadin: The four principles of "Americanism" were asserted in Margaret Chase Smith's "Declaration of Conscience" speech attacking this man.
question.text: Name this target of an attack by Joseph Welch.
question.clue: One president claimed that he "will not get into the gutter with ," whose popularity plummeted after he was asked "have you no sense of decency, sir" during a set of hearings.

swap.text: In the wake of this disaster, Reagan speechwriter Peggy Noonan wrote a speech quoting poet John Gillespie Magee that vowed to remember those that "slipped the surly bonds of earth" to "touch the face of God."
swap.clue: The Morton Thiokol Chemical Corporation was blamed for this event by the Rogers Commission investigating it, which included among its members Richard Feynman.

question.text: Before Stonewall, Mattachine Society hosted "sip-in's" at a bar with this name in New York. A scientist with this first name and his wife Ethel were the Rosenbergs executed for sending schematics to the Soviets in 1953.
question.clue: The most famous Pope with this name convoked the Fifth Lateran Council, created the League of Cambrai, and was the dedicatee of the Moses and Dying Slave sculpted in his namesake unfinished tomb.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the space race.
swap.text: Gagarin's space flight was a real kick in the teeth for the USA, who had been developing a program literally called "Man in Space Soonest". This man became the first American to go to space less than a month after Gagarin's orbit.
swap.clue: In May, 1961, this astronaut, who hit two golf balls while on the moon, became the first American in space.

question.text: This politician, who opposed neoconservative policies in H. W. Bush's cabinet would later embrace them as W. Bush's vice president.
question.clue: This man, who served as Vice President during George W. Bush's administration.

swap.leadin: In February of 2018, the US House passed an amendment to this act, which proponents hoped would end so-called "drive-by lawsuits."
swap.text: Name this act, originally passed in 1990, that prevents any discrimination based on disabilities. The proposed changes to this act would make it legal for business to not provide accessibility to disabled people until a specific complaint is filed.
swap.clue: In support of this law, 2nd grader Jennifer Keelan, along with many others, pulled themselves up all 100 stairs of the Capitol Building as part of the "Capitol Crawl."

question.leadin: Following a 1970s civil war, many people of this ethnicity settled in the communities of Eau Claire and Wausau, Wisconsin.
question.text: Name this ethnicity of nearly 400,000 Americans, many of whom came to the US after a "Secret War." In the 1980s, people of this ethnicity relocated from refugee camps to Merced.
question.answerHtml: Hmong Americans [or Hmoob Mes Kas; prompt on Miao, though this term is considered a pejorative)

swap.leadin: Answer the following about protests against the Vietnam War.
swap.text: In 1972, this actress protested the war with a much-criticized trip to Hanoi, where she was photographed on an anti-aircraft gun.
swap.clue: This American actress infamously expressed her opposition to the war by visiting North Vietnam. After getting photographed sitting on a North Vietnamese anti-aircraft gun, she was nicknamed "Hanoi."

question.leadin: During the London Blitz, this reporter opened his radio broadcasts with the phrase "This is London" before going on to describe the progress of the war.
question.text: Name this icon of American culture who proclaimed "We must not confuse dissent with disloyalty" in a later famous event.
question.clue: In 1935, as European bureau chief for CBS, he reported on the Nazi invasion of Austria and the London blitzkrieg.

swap.text: This man was the co-director and first chairman of the Tennessee Valley Authority, and also the first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission, in which role he co-authored a 1946 report on controlling atomic energy with Dean Acheson.
swap.answerHtml: David Eli <u>Lilienthal</u> [or David Eli <u>Lilienthal</u>; accept Acheson-<u>Lilienthal</u> Report]
swap.clue: This man's work Democracy on the March describes his clashes with Kenneth McKellar in establishing the corporation, which led to this man's nickname of "Mr. TVA." Truman later tapped him to serve as the first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission.

question.text: After the Great Peruvian Earthquake of 1970 triggered history's deadliest avalanche, the Velasco regime received the personal aid of this woman during their relief efforts. This woman and her husband had earlier been spit on and pelted with rocks during their visit to Venezuela.
question.answerHtml: Pat Nixon [or Thelma Nixon or Thelma Catherine Ryan; prompt on just Nixon] '

swap.leadin: This man, nicknamed the "Great Conciliator," was succeeded by Al Gore as Senator from Tennessee.
swap.text: Give this diplomat and moderate conservative. While serving on the Senate Watergate Committee, he famously asked, "What did the President know and when did he know it?"
